messages:
support-bot: New escalation from CS: customer 'acme-pay' reports p95/p99 jump on /v1/chat/generate since ~02:09 UTC. Rolling avg p99 1.8s -> 4.9s. Request rate normal. Ticket #INC-8823.
elaine: ack, looking. Any deploys or kernel changes pushed around 02:00-02:10?
raj: there was a canary that flipped an SDPA compile flag at 01:55 UTC to enable an optimized path on Ampere. Canary looked fine for 1h then gradually rolled at 02:05.
ben: seeing the same in infra alerts. p95 up from 300ms -> 1.2s. p99s exploded. I pulled a trace. Kernel selection logs show repeated fallthroughs to sdpa_v2 and then occasional fallback to flashpref.
ben: snippet from agent logs:
```
[02:06:12] kernel_selector: model=redwood-chat-3 seq=1024 prefer=flashpref available=[flashpref,sdpa_v2,sdpa_v1] chosen=sdpa_v2 reason=heuristic_cost
[02:06:12] sdpa_v2: compile_flags=--opt-level=3 --fuse-attn=true compile_time=3.2s
[02:06:12] runtime: kvcache/get hit=0.84 batch_wait=18ms latency_tail=5.1s
[02:09:03] kernel_selector: sdpa_v2 falling back -> flashpref due to kernel_error=OOM
```
raj: interesting: the compile flag enabled more aggressive fusion which reduces flops for many shapes but seems to make the runtime choose sdpa_v2 for long sequences. For some request patterns sdpa_v2 has pathological tail latency due to kernel scheduling + small batch sizes.
elaine: can we repro locally? steps and a simplified curl would help for CS.
raj: steps to repro (minimal):
1) model=redwood-chat-3; seq_len=1024; prompt that triggers long-kv usage (e.g., long context).
2) send 6 concurrent requests at ~20 qps from same instance to ensure small effective batch.
3) observe p99 using local perf harness `./perf_client --model redwood-chat-3 --seq 1024 --concurrency 6 --rps 20`

raj: quick check: toggle that compile flag back to opt-level=2 & disable fuse-attn. That made p99 drop in canary by ~60% earlier in our manual tests.
alex: tried the revert on one canary host (non-prod) and reproduced lower tails. Command I ran: `sudo env COMPILE_FLAGS="--opt-level=2 --fuse-attn=false" /srv/inference/reload-kernel --kernel sdpa_v2`
ben: ops note: we should avoid full rollback of the entire roll out until we confirm customer impact & mitigation. Suggested steps: (A) pin acme to fallback kernel (flashpref) via routing policy, (B) pause canary rollout, (C) patch compile flags and recompile sdpa_v2 with hysteresis logic, (D) increase batching window for affected fleet.
elaine: agree. Raj, can you create a hotpatch PR to add hysteresis (only pick sdpa_v2 if batch_wait < 40ms and batch_size >= 8)? Include a safety: if fallback_count > 3 within 60s then disqualify.
raj: on it. Draft branch: `kernels/sdpa-hysteresis-hotfix`. I'll also add telemetry counters to track fallback_count and kernel_queue_delay.
ben: CS asked for immediate mitigation. I just pushed a routing override to pin acme-pay requests to flashpref in region us-east-1. That will be in effect in ~20s.
support-bot: Routing override applied: route_id=rte-7739 target_kernel=flashpref scope=acme-pay region=us-east-1.
elaine: good. Ben, can you monitor p99 for acme specifically and share numbers in 10m?
ben: will do. Early numbers: acme p99 dropped from 4.9s -> 420ms after routing override. :thumbsup:
alex: ops follow-ups: schedule recompile on canary with opt-level=2 and run nightly perf regression to compare long-seq tails. Also add automated canary test with seq=1024 synthetic workload.
raj: PR opened: https://git.internal.redwood/kernels/pull/458 (sdpa hysteresis + telemetry). Requesting review from @elaine and @ben.
elaine: reviewing now. Also notify product about potential perf delta for some shapes.
ben: I'll leave a short postmortem draft in #postmortems once we stabilize. For now mitigation confirm: routing override + pause rollout + hotpatch PR + scheduled recompile.
support-bot: Escalation updated: status=mitigated scope=partial notes="acme pinned to flashpref; rollout paused; hotpatch PR opened" assigned=raj.
elaine: thanks team. Keep CS and customer updated: CS told acme we mitigated by routing them to fallback kernel and we're working on a fix.
raj: will follow up with telemetry graphs and a repro playbook.
ben: quick note — we'll need a unit test that simulates small-batch long-seq pathological case so we don't regress again.
elaine: agreed. End of thread for now; watch for PR merge and canary results.
